master.one_liner: Exact distance to the nearest Voronoi cell border (iq's two-pass method) plus bevel/plateau outputs; replaces the incorrect F2-F1 crackle.
master.look:
Prototype cl_cell mode 1 and 8: same polygon layout as F2-F1, but isolines are exact insets, so thresholds give even grout widths, and hillshade shows flat planar facets meeting at a straight skeleton like cut gems or hip roofs. Clean cracks, tiles, cobblestones, low-poly massifs.
[CellularEdge, dcc-tools] EdgeDistance: pyramids with truly constant-width dark borders, unlike F2-F1 on the sheet whose lines vary. Cobble: flagstone or stained glass with height per stone and rounded bevel. PackedDome: non-overlapping tangent bubbles and pebbles. Prototype: dcc_lens mode=12.
master.algorithm:
Pass 1 (3^d window, identical to CellularDistance F1): find nearest point: mr = r_nearest (vector sample->point), mg = its cell.
Pass 2 (window centred on mg, 5^d exact, or 3^d approx): for each cell g in window:
  r = (g + jitter(hash(mg+g)) - frac(p))      // vector to that cell's point
  diff = r - mr ; same = dot(diff,diff) < 1e-8 (mask)
  dEdge_candidate = dot(0.5*(mr + r), diff * InvSqrt(dot(diff,diff)))   // distance from p to the perpendicular bisector of mr and r
  dEdge = min(dEdge, Select(same, BIG, dEdge_candidate))
Output enum:
  EdgeDistance : dEdge (0 on borders, grows into the cell; C0 with creases on the medial axis)
  Bevel        : min(dEdge, BevelWidth)/BevelWidth (flat plateau cells with chamfered rims -> paving stones, dried mud plates)
  EdgeMask     : smoothstep(EdgeWidth, 0, dEdge) (crack lines of uniform width, unlike F2-F1 whose width varies with cell spacing)
  InscribedRadius: half the distance from the nearest point to its nearest neighbour (Blender's n-sphere radius) = min over pass 2 of 0.5*|diff|.
Distance metric for the bisector is Euclidean; a Manhattan/Chebyshev option is not exact, omit.
master.why_new: F2-F1 is 'pretty close' but wrong near cell corners and its line width depends on neighbour spacing; the exact border distance cannot be built from existing F-values because F2 changes discontinuously inside a cell. Needed for tiles, mud cracks, cracked ice, cobbles, Voronoi plateaus.
master.simd_plan: Two full 3^dim passes = 18/54/162 hashes, est 8 / 24 / 82 ns (2x CellularDistance). Euclidean only since bisectors are planar only then. Audit in 2D vs 7x7 brute force, 640k samples: FastNoise-style ring jitter, 3x3 second pass: radius 0.30 and below 0 wrong; 0.35 0.02% wrong (max err 0.05); 0.437 (kJitter2D) 0.96% wrong (max err 0.19). 5x5 second pass: 0 wrong even at full-cell jitter. So: 2D use 5x5 second pass (34 hashes, about 14 ns) or cap ring at 0.30; 3D/4D cap jitter.
master.continuity: EdgeDistance C0 with slope 1 (Lipschitz) when the window is sufficient; measured c0ratio 8.0 with square jitter <=0.7, and 1.1-1.8 at larger jitter due to missed neighbours. 3D at kJitter3D 0.396 ring with 3x3x3: 8.0 on one z slice, 6.48 on another, so nearly exact but not proven. CellRadius is cell-wise constant, discontinuous at borders. PackedDome is C0 because the disc fits inside the cell.
master.params: Feature Scale, Jitter Modifier, Second Pass Window enum {3 (fast), 5 (exact)}, Output enum {EdgeDistance, Bevel, EdgeMask, InscribedRadius}, Bevel Width / Edge Width (hybrid), Output Min/Max.
master.risks:
Jitter cap makes cells more regular than default CellularDistance, or 2D costs 3.5x. Size Jitter and non-Euclidean metrics cannot be supported. Sibling lens has related edge work; this entry adds the window audit numbers.
[CellularEdgeDistance, shader-community] 5^d second pass cost in 3D/4D; 3^d second pass gives rare wrong borders at high jitter. Size-jitter (grid jitter per cell) of the existing node is incompatible with exact bisectors; keep plain point jitter only.

shatter-bsp.look: Shattered glass / cracked ice: each Voronoi cell is cut by 2-3 straight cracks that stop dead at the cell wall or at their parent crack (real T-junctions), primary walls thick, children thinner (width decay). Leaf-value mode is a shard mosaic with strongly varied shard sizes and straight edges, unlike CellularValue. Tilt mode gives faceted rubble, bevel mode gives chamfered plates. At 5-6 levels the deeper cuts cluster into fans and thin slivers around each sub-cell centre (cuts pass near a tracked centre whose extents are unknown), so 3 levels with width decay 0.85 is the sweet spot; The comparison shows the fan problem at 6. Wide view (x2, x4) is isotropic with no lattice. The vol render shows 3D plates and shards; planes nearly parallel to a slice show as soft dark smears in 2D slices, which is correct for a sliced 3D crack field.

Thick primary cracks with thinner secondary cracks that stop dead at their parent (T junctions), which Voronoi cannot do because it only makes Y junctions. Leaf-value mode is a sharp shard mosaic; the tilted mode is rubble. Prototyped: rel_bsp, modes 0-4.
[ShatterBSP, lattice-kernels] Broken glass, shattered ice, drying mud with long cracks, faceted rock, tectonic plate maps. Prototyped with Voronoi base: strongly glass-like, no visible lattice. Brick base works but shows axis lines at base scale.
master.algorithm:
F1 + pass 2 gives owner p_i and wall = min_j (d_j^2-d_i^2)/(2|p_j-p_i|). Then for k=0..L-1 (constant loop): h=mix(h,k); n=unit vector from h; s=dot(x-c,n); if hash says active: crack=max(crack, depth_k*profile(|s|/w_k)); c += sign(s)*n*step_k; h=mix(h, s>0). Start c=p_i; step_k=0.42*0.62^k keeps the next cut inside the child; w_k and depth_k decay geometrically. Leaf id = final h. Because a leaf is convex and every bounding half-space is on the path, min(wall,|s_k|) is the true distance to the leaf boundary. Outputs: crack depth, leaf value, distance to boundary, per-leaf tilted plane.

[ShatterBSP, lattice-kernels] Base cell options: (a) Voronoi: F1 site, then d = min over window of the bisector distance dot(mid-x, n); (b) brick or hex with zero window, d = distance to base edges. Then local u = x - site, c = 0, r = 0.5, id = base hash. for l in 0..Depth-1 (constant): h = mix(id, l); gate = h01 < CutProb; n = gradient table[h bits]; off = rnd11*0.4*r; s = dot(u-c, n) - off; d = Select(gate, min(d,|s|), d); side = sign(s); c += gate*n*(off + side*r/2); r *= gate ? 0.72 : 1; id = mix(h, side bit). Output modes: EdgeDistance = 1-2*sat(d/Cap), CellValue = rnd11(id), or the product of the two. The distance is exact because for a point inside a convex polygon the distance to the boundary equals the min distance to its supporting lines, and redundant cuts are only further away.
master.why_new: F2-F1 has only Y junctions, a single scale and tapering walls. Layering two cellular nodes gives lines that cross instead of stopping. Hierarchical stopping needs the path-dependent state here, and no node exposes it.
master.simd_plan: All masks, Depth is constant. Each level: 1 hash mix, 1 table lookup, 1 dot, 2 Selects. Depth 5 costs about one Perlin in 2D, and is dimension independent apart from dot size. Voronoi base: about 2x CellularDistance (F1 pass plus bisector pass), so 8-10 ns 2D, 28 ns 3D. Brick base: 2 ns 2D, 3 ns 3D, 5 ns 4D. GenT generic is straightforward. Measured scalar with 5x5 Voronoi base: 6x perlin2.
master.continuity: Crack and distance outputs are C0 provided depth_k decreases with k: at a level-k cut both sides share all ancestors and value depth_k dominates deeper ones. Verified c0ratio 8.00 in 2D and smooth z in 3D. Leaf value and tilted plane are discontinuous by design.

master.risks:
Cuts are unbalanced, so slivers appear (visible but they read as natural fracture). A hybrid Crack Width varying fast may break depth ordering. Without the Voronoi top level the lattice shows as straight grid lines, so the F1 cost cannot be dropped.
[ShatterBSP, lattice-kernels] With a 3x3 bisector window a missing distant neighbour could overestimate d near far corners; capping d (Cap < 0.5 cell) hides it, needs measuring. Tree tends to many thin triangles at high Depth: shrinking off range or biasing the cut normal to the longest axis would need tracking cell extents.
[StitCrystalCellular, lit-recent] Split planes chosen through the base cell may produce cells with the base-grid square outline visible (jitter the base grid by a hashed per-cell offset or make the first split cut the grid cell at a random position to hide it). Exact EdgeDistance only counts planes in the ancestry, which is exact for the cell's own boundary but ignores planes of neighbouring cells that stop at a T-junction (harmless: those are not boundaries of this cell).
master.cost_note: Voronoi base: about 2x CellularDistance (F1 pass plus bisector pass), so 8-10 ns 2D, 28 ns 3D.

master.one_liner: Window-free tile node: base bond (grid, running bond, basket, herringbone) plus recursive per-tile KD splits, with exact edge distance and a per-tile source frame for parquet, ashlar and planks.
master.look:
Look-tested (m=11). Rich ashlar or city-block tiling and a very convincing parquet where each plank has its own wood slice and rotation. Axis-aligned, nothing like the Voronoi family. Warps make hand-laid stone, and fractal stacks make circuit-board or greeble maps.
[MondrianTree, hierarchy-multiscale] Rectilinear rooms and streets with multi-size tiles, greeble panels, PCB layouts, floorplans. Very unlike everything on the contact sheet except Checkerboard.
master.algorithm:
Base bond: row jr=floor(y), tx=x+Bond*(jr odd), ir=floor(tx/BrickW), bounds [x0,x1]x[y0,y1], h=hash(ir,jr). Herringbone and basket use a small mod 4 table for bounds and id. Loop L levels (constant): h=mix(h,l); stop mask if rnd<Stop (frozen via Select); split axis by comparing size*rnd per axis (longer axis favoured, RowBias); cut m=lo+size*(Bal+(1-2Bal)*rnd). Select lower or upper side, update bound and h. After loop: e=Min over axes of (p-lo, hi-p), exact distance to own rectangle, T-junctions automatically correct. Local frame l=p-centre. Outputs by Mode: tone(h); bevel smoothstep(0,Bevel,e)*tone; Interior: eval source once at R90(h)*l + offset(h), times bevel. Parquet = TileSplit(Interior=Strata(GrowthAge)).

[MondrianTree, hierarchy-multiscale] Root box=floor(p/RootSize) cell; val=k*min distance to box faces; id=hash(cell). For L=1..Depth: h=mix(id,L). Split mask: rnd(h)<SplitProb(L), or Density.Gen at the box centre remapped to a probability. Split axis = longest box side (Select across axes). t=0.3+0.4*rnd(h>>8); c=lerp(bmin[a],bmax[a],t); d=p[a]-c. Update bmin/bmax by Select. val=min(val, Age*L+k*|d|). id=mix(id,d>0). Output: Crack, Leaf=rnd(id), Plate=rnd(id)*smoothstep(0,w,val), Bump=Leaf window times Source sampled in leaf coordinates (detail always vanishes at leaf edges, so per-leaf changes cannot seam).
master.why_new: Per-tile source frames do not exist anywhere: CellularLookup gives a constant per cell, and domain ops cannot jump per-tile. No search, so cost is independent of dimension: 4D costs barely more than 2D, unlike every cell node. Exact edge distance gives clean bevels.
master.simd_plan: L levels each with one mix, a few Selects and compares, no sqrt. Scalar 2.3x Perlin at L=3 including the mode hash; AVX2 about 1-2x Perlin in 2D. Dimension agnostic: GenT over pack with axis choice via argmax of size*rnd and Select per axis. 3D and 4D about 1.3x and 1.6x of 2D, making this far cheaper than Perlin 4D. Interior adds exactly one source eval.
master.continuity: Crack is C0, measured at c0ratio 8.00 with max slope 12. Leaf is discontinuous by design. Plate and Bump are C0.
master.params: Bond enum, Brick Width, Bond Offset, Levels (int), Stop, Balance, Row Bias, Bevel, Mode enum, Interior (generator), Interior Rotation enum, Interior Offset. Hybrid: Stop, Balance, Bevel (splits may vary across space, which moves walls, so document it).
master.risks:
Another lens has also explored BSP-style splitting (rel_bsp), so the new parts here are the bond table and Interior frame. Hybrid Balance shifts cut lines smoothly, but crossing a stop threshold creates a jump. Torus tiling works numerically but rectangles become curved.
[MondrianTree, hierarchy-multiscale] The root grid is visible in the proto as lines of constant period. Mitigate with large root cells and small Age at level 0, or suggest a domain warp input. Axis alignment is the feature, but the FFT will show a strong cross. A Density hybrid sampled at the pixel would jump, so it must be evaluated at the box centre.
master.cost_note: Scalar 2.3x Perlin at L=3 including the mode hash; AVX2 about 1-2x Perlin in 2D. 3D and 4D about 1.3x and 1.6x of 2D, making this far cheaper than Perlin 4D.
master.variant_notes: Axis-aligned KD descent with no window, so cost barely rises to 4D. MondrianTree adds source-driven split density evaluated at the box centre, not the lane.

Merged walls at kd 0.8 are closed plates, at 0.2-0.3 they leave short tapered stubs at vertices, at 0.05-0.1 long gray smears. The rule is that width / kd must stay small enough for the window to see the other colour: kd 0.2 at width 0.05 gave 0 jumps, kd 0.1 gave 14 of 3M with 2 colours, kd 0.05 gave 22. master.one_liner: Voronoi using true bisector distances and a commutative per-edge hash, so each wall gets its own width, depth or absence: real crack networks, rounded pebbles, curled mud plates.
master.look: Look-tested (m=4). Dropped edges make non-convex polygons and dangling crack ends, which reads far more like dried mud or glaze crazing than F2-F1. Width varies per crack and stays constant along it. Pebble mode gives rounded stones with clean gaps; plate mode gives raised curled tiles with sharp fractures. Covers leather (pebble with low Dome and warp), stucco, cobbles, hex tiles.
master.algorithm: Pass 1: F1 search in 3x3 giving site a, hash ha and cell index. Pass 2: for neighbours b of the F1 cell, n=norm(b-a), d_b=dot(mid(a,b)-p,n) (true distance to that bisector, positive). Edge hash e=mix(ha ^ hb) is symmetric, so both sides agree. Fate=rnd(e): an edge exists if fate>Drop, with width w_e=W*(.25+.75*rnd(mix e)). Modes: Crack: c=Max over live edges of (1-d_b/w_e), output profile of c. Pebble: soft distance sd=(sum d_b^-p)^(-1/p) with p=4,6,8 (order independent), t=sat((sd-Gap)/Dome), height sqrt(t*(2-t))*tone(ha). Plate: per-cell tilted plane tone(ha)+dot(tilt(ha),p-a)+Curl*(1-sat(sd/Rim)), then lerp toward CrackDepth by c. Lattice enum: Square, Staggered (row offset 0.5 gives honeycomb and hex tile at low jitter).
master.why_new: F2-F1 is not a true distance, so its walls change width along their length, and it has no notion of an edge as an object. The symmetric pair hash is the new primitive: per-edge attributes without any global data. The reciprocal power sum gives rounded polygons without smin ordering artifacts.
master.simd_plan: Pass 1 is 9 candidates as today. Pass 2 uses 8 neighbours around per-lane F1 index (hash from lane integer coords works). Total 17 distance-class evals, about 2x CellularDistance 2D (scalar proto used 24 neighbours and measured 10x Perlin). 3D: 27+26 evals, about 2x CellularDistance 3D. 4D: 81+80, about 2x CellularDistance 4D, expensive but works, so tiling is real. d^-p by multiplication; root via Sqrt chain for p=4 and 8. master.continuity: Crack and Pebble are C0 apart from tiny jumps near triple points where a live edge term differs between sides (measured c0ratio 1.25 cracks at very high slope, 2.83 pebbles). master.one_liner: Worley cells whose crease (wall) depth is driven by the difference of a Region source sampled at the two cells' sites, giving hierarchical crack networks with real T-junctions (leather, dry mud, elephant skin, cobbles in flagstone groups, tectonic terraces) from a single Worley pass.
master.look: Polygonal cells separated by V or U creases whose depth varies in a structured way: wide deep cracks outline groups of cells, fine shallow creases subdivide them, ends meet in T-junctions, exactly like dried mud, old leather, elephant skin, crackle glaze or flagstone paving with sand joints. PlateauMinusCrease gives stepped mesas with fissures along the steps. Distinct from F2-F1 (uniform width, no hierarchy) and from STIT cuts (straight, no polygon cells).
master.algorithm:
Params: Region (HybridSource; constant => uniform crease), Base, Gain, Width W (hybrid, cell units <=0.5), Profile power P (hybrid), WallJitter, Lift, Mode {Crease, PlateauMinusCrease, RegionOfNearest}, ExactJunctions bool, jitter, distance function.

Window 3^d around the sample like CellularDistance. Pass 1: for each cell j compute site c_j, d_j = dist(p, c_j); keep d1 = min, nearest index n, c_n. Evaluate R_n = Region(c_n). Pass 2 (recompute sites and distances; cheaper than spilling 27 registers in 3D): for each j != n: R_j = Region(c_j) (3^d Source evals at the site positions, so they are per-point constants and never pop); D_jn = clamp(Base + Gain*|R_j - R_n| + WallJitter*rnd01(hash(min(h_j,h_n), max(h_j,h_n))), 0, 1) (symmetric by construction); t = (d_j - d1)/W; g = max(0, 1 - t)^P; h = max(h, D_jn * g).
Output: Crease: 1 - 2h. PlateauMinusCrease: Lift*R_n - 2h (stepped plateaus whose risers are cracks: terraces where the Region field is terraced). RegionOfNearest: R_n (flat per-cell value of the region field, for masks).

Why difference-of-region: with Region = Terrace(low-frequency noise) you get discrete parents, child walls lying on parent boundaries are deep, interior walls shallow, and the child walls meet the parent walls in T-junctions because the parent walls ARE child walls. With Region = smooth noise the depth is proportional to the local gradient across the wall (graded creases). With Region = Gradient along a direction the creases perpendicular to that direction open wider: anisotropic shrinkage cracks, bark fissures, stretched paint. With Region = coarse CellularValue you get true nested Voronoi (fibre bundles, flagstone groups).

ExactJunctions option: h = max over pairs (j,k) in the window of D_jk * g(|d_j - d_k|/W) * g2((min(d_j,d_k) - d1)/W). Every factor is continuous in p, so the output is strictly C0 at triple junctions where three different regions meet (the cheaper nearest-referenced form can jump by at most D_ab there). 36 pairs in 2D (cheap, no sqrt), 351 in 3D (offer only in 2D/extruded).
master.why_new: CellularDistance gives one uniform crease; CellularValue gives flat cells. No graph can make a wall's depth depend on a property of the two cells it separates, and no existing node yields nested Voronoi with consistent T-junctions in one pass. The Region source makes one node cover leather, mud, bark, flagstone and terraced terrain.
master.simd_plan: Two passes over the standard 3^d window with masks, same structure as Cellular.inl; the second pass does 3^d Region evaluations at site positions (int32v seed unchanged, positions are the jittered sites). 2D/3D/4D generic over the pack. Cost: 2D about Worley 3.9 + 9x(Region) + 1 ns (Perlin Region: ~15 ns; constant Region: ~5 ns); 3D 12 + 27x(Region); 4D 41 + 81x(Region), expensive but it works and tiles. Keep W <= 0.5 so the 3x3 window is as exact as F2.
master.continuity: C0 in Crease mode away from triple junctions where three distinct regions meet (nearest-referenced form: bounded jump <= D_ab there, usually invisible); strictly C0 with ExactJunctions. PlateauMinusCrease is discontinuous at walls only by the amount Lift*(R_a - R_b), which is exactly the step you asked for; RegionOfNearest is piecewise constant.
master.params: Region (hybrid source, the heart of it), Base, Gain, Width (hybrid), Profile power (hybrid), WallJitter, Lift, Mode enum, ExactJunctions, Jitter, DistanceFunction (reuse CalcDistance).
master.risks: Window exactness identical to F2 (jitter <= 0.437, W <= 0.5). 3D with a noisy Region is 27 Source evals; recommend Region = cheap Value/Perlin or a constant. The proto must measure the junction jump of the cheap form before deciding whether ExactJunctions is needed in 2D by default.
master.cost_note: Cost: 2D about Worley 3.9 + 9x(Region) + 1 ns (Perlin Region: ~15 ns; constant Region: ~5 ns); 3D 12 + 27x(Region); 4D 41 + 81x(Region), expensive but it works and tiles.

master.one_liner: Crystal grains grown from seeds: each grain has its own random orientation and polyhedral growth shape, and the field is arrival time of the growth front.
master.look:
Prototyped. 3D isosurface T<0.15: clusters of sharp faceted rhombic-dodecahedral crystals in random orientations, the most striking render in this batch; superb for geodes, ice, gems, sci-fi crystals. 2D slice: angular pyramids with random tilted polygon shapes, each differently oriented; Zoned mode gives concentric tilted polygons like a Vasarely print or mineral thin-section. Threshold over time animates crystal growth with no 4D lattice.
[CrystalCells, nature-phenomena] Hillshade shows flat faces and straight creases, like cut gems, low-poly rock or quartz clusters, with nothing curved. Zoned output gives concentric pentagons and hexagons clipped by neighbours, like agate or zoned feldspar. The 3D isosurface should give faceted polyhedra, but that was not rendered.
master.algorithm:
Window 3^dim, jittered sites. For each site: v = p-s_i; orient via two Householder reflections with normals from hash bit fields (v -= 2(n.v)n, twice), giving a rotation with no matrix table; gauge = Wulff shape norm of v, options cube max|v_i|, octahedron (sum|v_i|)/sqrt(3), rhombic dodecahedron max(|x|+|y|,|y|+|z|,|x|+|z|)/sqrt(2); T_i = gauge/(1 + Rate*rnd11) + T0*rnd01 (Johnson-Mehl-Avrami nucleation delay). T = min T_i, tracking second. Output enum: Time (T), Boundary (T2-T1), Zoned sin(T*Zones) for growth banding like agate or zoned feldspar, GrainValue. Normalise by a measured constant.

[CrystalGrainNoise, volumetric-3d4d] Window 3x3x3 (3x3 2D). Per cell k: h = Hash(k); c = k + 0.5 + Jitter*rnd3(h); tau = Delay * rnd01(h>>8); R = RotTable[(h>>12) & 31] (32 random rotation matrices from unit quaternions; 2D: 32 angles); speed v = 1 - SpeedJitter*rnd01(h>>17); habit = node enum or per-grain from bits.
 q = R * (p - c)
 norm: Sphere |q|; Cube Max(|qx|,|qy|,|qz|)*1.24; Octahedron (|qx|+|qy|+|qz|)*0.72; HexPrism Max( Max_j |q.d_j| (d_j at 0,60,120 deg in xy), |qz|*k ); RhombicDodeca Max over 6 normals (1,1,0)/sqrt2 perms of |q.n| (constants chosen so the unit ball volumes match the sphere)
 T = tau + norm / v
 keep T1, T2 (two-value insertion via Min/Max masks) and the hash of the T1 winner
Outputs enum: Age = T1 scaled over [0, Tmax]; Boundary = T2 - T1 (0 at grain walls); GrainValue = rnd11(winner); AgeInGrain = (T1 - tau_winner) (a faceted distance inside each crystal). Cap Delay <= 0.5 to keep the 3x3x3 window valid (same imprecision class as existing Cellular with full jitter).
master.why_new: Manhattan and MaxAxis metrics exist but share one global orientation, so all facets align (see the Cellular Manhattan tile, aligned diamonds). Per-grain orientation plus a Wulff gauge cannot be expressed by nodes, since metric rotation per cell is internal to the search. Growth delay gives curved grain boundaries that no existing jitter does.
master.simd_plan: Same window as CellularDistance plus two reflections per site (6 mul-adds and 3 hash field extractions per reflection) and abs/max for the gauge. No sqrt needed for the polyhedral gauge, offsetting some cost. Estimate 1.5x to 2x CellularDistance: 6 / 20 / 75 ns. Scalar prototype with quaternions was 9.65x perlin2, 4.3x worley2, and the reflections are cheaper. 4D is expensive but needed only for tiling; for animation use Time with threshold.
master.continuity: C0: a min of continuous functions. Dense scanlines: 0 jumps, worst step near zero. Creases are C0 by design.
master.params: Gauge enum, Rate (hybrid), T0 (hybrid), Zones (float), GridJitter, Output enum.
master.risks:
Window correctness: gauge can be smaller than Euclidean so a site outside the 3^dim window could win in rare cases; keep jitter <= 0.45 and rate moderate, then run seam check (none seen by eye). Rate spread is a size-limiting factor. Facets alias when thin; normals need sharp isosurface extraction, so meshers without feature preservation will round them.
[CrystalGrainNoise, volumetric-3d4d] Rotation table via gather is slow on SSE paths; use 8-entry Select trees. Delay > 0.5 makes window seams. Polyhedral norms are not Euclidean so AgeInGrain is faceted by design but Boundary walls get kinks.
[CrystalCells, nature-phenomena] Large delay can let a seed outside the window win, causing seams; keep delay within about 0.6 cell at 3x3 (the prototype used 0.6, and an earlier 5x5 run used 0.5). Per-cell 3D rotation choice affects look. Output range depends on face count and needs a measured constant. Johnson-Mehl literature covers tessellations in general; its use as a texture metric is my extension.

recursive-cut-noise.look: The family question, proven (root sweep at a 12-unit window): with no root, level 0 is one global family of parallel lines for the whole seed, and every wide view shows long parallel strips with cross cuts (also the FFT is a star). A square grid root replaces that with a visible square lattice. Only the Voronoi root gives an isotropic shatter, and with it the node is ShatterBSP with line families instead of single cuts. Line families have their own problem: at lacunarity >= 1.3 a family crosses an elongated sub-cell several times and hatches it with parallel lines (the lacunarity grid); at f=1, lac=1.15 with per-strip boundary jitter 0.5 the look matches ShatterBSP almost exactly apart from occasional close parallel pairs. So the two unique selling points (dimension-independent cost, no window) only hold for the version that looks bad.

master.one_liner: Stateless recursive hyperplane cuts: a fixed loop that gives shattered-glass, Mondrian and crack patterns with real T-junctions, at a cost independent of dimension.
master.look: Prototype cl_cut sheet (levels 7, Ratio 1.41, Skip .3): stained glass, smashed window, angular shards; the 3D XZ slice works directly. AxisAligned: Mondrian panels, city blocks, circuit boards, glitch rects. Crack output for dried mud, crazed glaze, fault lines. FFT is a star of streaks, utterly unlike the rest of the sheet.
master.algorithm:
id=seed; f=F0; d=inf.
for level l in 0..Levels-1:
  h=mix(id,l)
  keep = rnd(h) >= Skip  (mask)
  w = direction from h: table of unit vectors, or one axis in AxisAligned mode
  t = dot(w,x)*f + phi(h)
  fl=Floor(t); fr=t-fl
  dl=min(fr,1-fr)/f
  d=Select(keep, min(d,dl), d)
  id=Select(keep, mix(id ^ int(fl)*PrimeX, l), id)
  f*=Ratio  (1.41 halves cell area per level)
The next level's lines depend on the parent cell id, so a line stops at its parent's border: T-junctions, which Worley cells cannot make.
Output enum: Crack = saturate(d/Width)*2-1. CellValue = rnd(mix(id)). Value x crack. Plane tilt = dot(hashdir,x-local) per cell.
Optional root: id0 from nearest Voronoi site (one Cellular search) so level-0 lines are not global.
master.why_new: All existing cell nodes are Voronoi: convex cells, Y-junctions, no hierarchy. Hyperplane recursion gives long straight lines, T-junctions and wide cell size variety. It is also the only cell pattern whose cost does not rise with dimension. Guehl et al. list iterative cell subdivision imitating STIT tessellations as a new cellular noise; this version needs no precomputed wave table.
master.simd_plan: Per level: hash, direction lookup, dot, Floor, 2 Selects, ~25-30 ops, ~.35 ns. Levels=7: ~2.5 ns in 2D (2.3x Perlin) and about the same in 4D (0.7x Perlin, 16x cheaper than CellularDistance 4D). Pure GenT<P...>; id is per lane int32v, so no masks beyond keep. Scalar 4x perlin2 at L=6, using trig the port replaces with a table.
master.continuity: Crack output C0, c0ratio 7.2-7.8: d is 0 on both sides of a crossed line, and inside a convex cell it is the min of plane distances. CellValue is discontinuous by design (Output Min/Max range still holds).
master.params: Int: Levels. Float: F0, Ratio. Hybrid: Skip, Width. Enum: Direction (Random, AxisAligned, K-fold), Output. Optional Width taper per level.
master.risks: Level-0 lines are global and parallel for a given seed, a visible bias at wide views unless the Voronoi root option is used. Deep levels make slivers and dust if Ratio is above about 1.5 (seen at 1.5/1.6). Line spacing per family is regular, so a jittered 1D line version with 3 Selects may be needed. Hard edges alias. Thresholds need Width taper tuning.

master.one_liner: Exact distance to Voronoi walls (uniform width) combined with per-cell radial cracks that stop at the walls, per-wall width from a symmetric pair hash, plus 'order-2 / order-3 Voronoi' region ids (each cell shattered into convex sectors by which neighbour is second closest).
master.look: Shattered glass / cracked ice: uniform-width Voronoi walls (F2-F1 walls thin out where walls meet at acute angles; these do not) with extra straight cracks radiating from each cell centre and terminating exactly at the walls. Order-2 value shows every cell split into kite-shaped pie pieces facing each neighbour, a 'mosaic within mosaic' that no existing value mode produces.
master.algorithm:
Pass 1 (Cellular loop): F1 point P1 with v1 = S - P1, F2, F3 hashes and distances.
Pass 2 over the same window (positions kept in an array):
  for each j != F1: n = P_j - P1; wall_j = (dot(v1, n) - 0.5*dot(n,n)) * InvSqrt(dot(n,n))   // signed distance from S to the bisector, true distance to that wall
  t_j = WidthMul(Hash(min(h1,hj), max(h1,hj)))  // symmetric pair hash, 0.5..1.5
  W = min_j wall_j / t_j
  (continuity argument: at the wall between a and b the term for the other cell is 0 on both sides, so min is 0 from both sides; inside a cell all terms are continuous)
Radial cracks: K unit directions u_{c,k} from a table indexed by hash bits of the F1 cell, k = 0..K-1 (K constant):
  tk = max(0, dot(v1, u_k)); ray_k = |v1 - tk*u_k| ; ray_k = Select(tk > RayLen, |v1| - ..., ray_k) (optional finite length)
  C = min(W, min_k ray_k / RayWidthMul)  (C0: at a wall W = 0 dominates on both sides)
Outputs: WallDistance = W (clamped at Dmax), Cracks = C, Order2Value = rnd11(SymHash(h1,h2)), Order3Value = rnd11(SymHash3(h1,h2,h3)), SectorValue = rnd11(hash(h1, sector)) with sector = bitmask of sign(cross(u_k, v1)) over K directions.
3D: identical formulas with 3-vectors; radial cracks become rays (use 'crack planes' through P1 with random normal: |dot(v1, n_k)| for planar fracture faces).
master.why_new: Exact wall distance is a known shader trick (IQ) missing from FastNoise; the radial cracks are continuous only because of the min-with-wall argument; order-k region ids cost nothing beyond the hashes already computed yet give a genuinely new partition.
master.simd_plan: Two passes over the 3x3 / 3x3x3 window: first the normal Cellular F1..F3 search (store relative positions and hashes in arrays), second pass computing wall_j (dot, fnmadd, rsqrt, mul: ~8 ops) and pair hash (~6 ops) per point; rays K x ~8 ops. 2D ~8 ns (2x Cellular2D), 3D ~25 ns, 4D ~80 ns. Fully branch-free; the min/Select chain replaces per-lane early-out.
master.continuity: WallDistance and Cracks: C0 (proof in algorithm). Order/Sector values: discontinuous flat fills.
master.params: Output enum {WallDistance, Cracks, Order2Value, Order3Value, SectorValue}, Crack Count K (int 0..6), Ray Width (hybrid), Wall Width Jitter, Crack Length, Grid Jitter (hybrid), Distance Function (for F ordering only), Feature Scale.
master.risks: Per-wall width must be symmetric and finite; removing walls entirely is discontinuous in this dual formulation (use CellularDualMesh for mazes). Radial crack directions are per cell, so cracks on opposite sides of a wall do not line up (looks fine for glass, wrong for continuous fractures).
